name: Palbociclib
route_note: oral capsule or tablet once daily for 21 days of 28-day cycles, with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant

discovery.by: Parke-Davis/Pfizer (Peter Toogood and colleagues); preclinical breast cancer work by Dennis Slamon and Richard Finn at UCLA
discovery.note: A pyridopyrimidine highly selective for CDK4 and CDK6, shelved for years until UCLA studies showed activity in oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer cells.

tagline: First CDK4/6 inhibitor, doubling progression-free time in HR+ advanced breast cancer
summary: Palbociclib is an oral, selective inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 that halts the cell cycle in G1. Combined with endocrine therapy, it roughly doubles progression-free survival in hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer and was the first CDK4/6 inhibitor approved.
mechanism: In oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer, oestrogen signalling induces cyclin D1, which activates CDK4/6. These kinases phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein (RB), releasing E2F transcription factors that drive entry into S phase.

Palbociclib blocks CDK4/6, keeping RB hypophosphorylated and arresting cells in G1; combined endocrine therapy produces deeper growth suppression. Tumours lacking functional RB are resistant. Inhibition of CDK6 in haematopoietic precursors causes reversible neutropenia.
uses: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with an aromatase inhibitor (first endocrine therapy) or with fulvestrant (after endocrine therapy)
With inavolisib and fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated advanced breast cancer

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Compound discovered at Parke-Davis, which Pfizer acquires in 2000 through Warner-Lambert.

history.title: UCLA preclinical work
history.detail: Finn, Slamon and colleagues show luminal ER-positive breast cancer cell lines are most sensitive.

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves palbociclib with letrozole based on PALOMA-1.

history.title: With fulvestrant
history.detail: Approval with fulvestrant after endocrine therapy (PALOMA-3).

history.title: Full approval
history.detail: PALOMA-2 confirms benefit with letrozole; EU approval in 2016.

history.title: Tablet formulation
history.detail: Tablet formulation approved that can be taken with or without food.

history.title: Inavolisib combination
history.detail: FDA approves inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated disease.

facts: Unlike chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, CDK4/6-inhibitor neutropenia rarely causes febrile infection because it reflects arrest rather than death of precursors.
